CVE-2025-35939.title: Craft CMS stores user-provided content in session files
CVE-2025-35939.description: Craft CMS stores arbitrary content provided by unauthenticated users in session files. This content could be accessed and executed, possibly using an independent vulnerability. Craft CMS redirects requests that require authentication to the login page and generates a session file on the server at '/var/lib/php/sessions'. Such session files are named 'sess_[session_value]', where '[session_value]' is provided to the client in a 'Set-Cookie' response header. Craft CMS stores the return URL requested by the client without sanitizing parameters. Consequently, an unauthenticated client can introduce arbitrary values, such as PHP code, to a known local file location on the server. Craft CMS versions 5.7.5 and 4.15.3 have been released to address this issue.

kev.name: Craft CMS External Control of Assumed-Immutable Web Parameter Vulnerability

CVE-2026-112880.title: CRLF injection in Proxy-Authorization header built from proxy_auth_fun in hackney
CVE-2026-112880.description:
Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences in HTTP Headers ('HTTP Request/Response Splitting') vulnerability in hackney_http_connect in benoitc hackney allows HTTP Request Splitting via the value a proxy_auth_fun callback returns. After a 407 response from an HTTP CONNECT proxy, hackney_http_connect:handle_proxy_auth/11 calls the caller's proxy_auth_fun with the status code and the response headers and writes the returned binary into the Proxy-Authorization line of the CONNECT retry without checking it. A CR, LF or NUL byte in that value adds header lines to the request sent to the proxy.

The value is attacker-influenced when the callback derives it from untrusted data, for example from the proxy's challenge headers. Other caller-supplied values on the CONNECT path, such as the target host and the request headers, were already checked for control bytes.

This issue affects hackney: from 2.0.0 before 4.9.0.

CVE-2026-98942.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

sched_ext: Build the cid tables privately and publish them with RCU

The cid tables are visible to the cid kfuncs while being modified: the
first enable publishes the global pointers before filling them,
ops.init_cids() overrides rewrite them in place, and re-enables rebuild
them in place. A racing TRACING or SYSCALL program can read unfilled
entries, including uninitialized memory in the kmalloc'd tables, or torn
topo updates.

Tie the tables' lifetimes to the root sched instead: each root enable
builds a fresh set privately and publishes the per-table __rcu globals once
the layout is final, and root disable unpublishes and RCU-frees the set. A
non-NULL global is now always a fully built table which stays valid for the
reader's RCU read section, and lookups stay two loads. Kfuncs treat NULL as
no-mapping, also after the scheduler exits instead of reporting the stale
last mapping.

CVE-2026-99101.title: ntfs: move attribute payload before shrinking its record
CVE-2026-99101.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ntfs: move attribute payload before shrinking its record

ntfs_new_attr_flags() resizes the non-resident attribute record before
moving its name and mapping pairs to their shorter-header offsets when
compression or sparse state is cleared.

Shrinking the record first moves the following attribute over the tail of
the old record. The subsequent memmove() therefore copies bytes from that
following attribute instead of the old mapping pairs. Re-enabling
compression on an empty file persists those bytes as a malformed mapping
pairs array, which ntfsck reports as a missing or invalid run length.

Move the payload before shrinking the record, while retaining the existing
resize-before-move ordering when growing it.

CVE-2026-99651.title: mm/ksm: reset the unstable trees of all nodes
CVE-2026-99651.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/ksm: reset the unstable trees of all nodes

Each full scan resets ksm_nr_node_ids unstable tree roots. Enabling
merge_across_nodes resets this count to 1, even if per-node roots were
previously allocated.

So when toggling "merge_across_nodes" 0 -> 1 -> 0, a scan that starts
while the setting is 1 and continues after switching back to 0 can
encounter stale unstable tree roots, resulting in UAF.

Only root is allowed to change "merge_across_nodes", and the documented
sequence is: "merge_across_nodes setting can be changed only when there
are no ksm shared pages in the system: set run 2 to unmerge pages first,
then to 1 after changing merge_across_nodes, to remerge according to the
new setting."

Let's fix it by tracking in ksm_nr_node_ids the actual number of
allocated tree roots.

remove_all_stable_nodes() and ksm_check_stable_tree() will now scan
more tree roots (skipping the empty ones), which is harmless.
